previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after developing worsening pain and drainage from a second-degree burn on her left lower leg sustained from spilled boiling pudding. Due to her wheelchair dependence and body habitus, she was unable to remove the hot liquid promptly. She was treated with unroofing of the burn by plastic surgery, daily Silvadene dressings, and antibiotics—IV Unasyn and oral linezolid—due to a vancomycin allergy. She remained afebrile with stable vitals. Her INR dropped to subtherapeutic levels, likely due to antibiotic interaction, prompting initiation of Lovenox bridging therapy, which successfully restored therapeutic anticoagulation. All chronic conditions, including HIV, hepatitis B and C, heart failure, asthma, and chronic pain, were managed with home medications. She improved clinically, completed necessary treatments, and was discharged home with services to continue antibiotics, wound care, and anticoagulation.

Portable AP chest radiograph was reviewed in comparison to prior study from

The PICC line appears to be looped in the left axilla and should be
repositioned.  The heart size is normal.  Lungs are well aerated.  Diffuse
interstitial opacities seen on the prior study within the lungs, in particular
lung bases, are minimal and unchanged.  Linear atelectasis is seen in the left
lung base.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

There is persistent right upper lobe opacity in the paramediastinal location. 
It can be seen on the several prior radiographs including CT torso from ___.  Although it might represent nonresolving infectious process, it also
can be due to a neoplastic focus, thus repeated evaluation with chest CT is
suggested to exclude this possibility.

PROCEDURE:  Placement of left-sided midline single lumen 4 ___ catheter.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with morbid obesity, requires intravenous access
for outpatient antibiotic therapy.  The patient has had previous PICC lines
all of which were midline only and a guide wire has never successfully been
passed beyond the level of the axillary vein on either side.  Of note, the
patient has an iodine contrast allergy to performance of a diagnostic
venogram.

ANESTHESIA:  1%  lidocaine was administered to the skin around the
venopuncture site.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.  Dr. ___, the
attending radiologist, supervised the procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Informed verbal consent was obtained after outlining
the risks and benefits of the procedure involved.  Following this, the patient
was brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.
The left upper limb and existing catheter were prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.  A preprocedure huddle and timeout were performed as per
___ protocol.

Ultrasound of left upper limb confirms satisfactory position of the previous
catheter within the left basilic vein.  Passage of an 0.018 nitinol wire
through the catheter would not advance further than the left axillary vein
level.  Given the iodine contrast allergy, venogram was not possible.
Ultrasound with copy images on file confirmed a patent left brachial vein.  A
decision was made to access this vein to try and navigate an alternative
venous course centrally. Following administration of 1% lidocaine, the left
brachial vein was accessed with a micropuncture needle.  Again an 0.018
nitinol wire was advanced through the wire and passed again to the level of
the left axillary vein where no further progress could be made.  The team was
contacted and decision was made to place a midline catheter for antibiotic
therapy. Appropriate measurements were made and a new 22-cm single lumen 4
___ PICC line was advanced through the existing access via the left basilic
vein.  The tip lies in the axillary vein.  The catheter was aspirated,
flushed, and secured with an adhesive dressing.  The catheter may be used
immediately for infusion therapy.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a 22-cm midline catheter via the left
basilic vein.  Catheter measures 22 cm in length and is 4 ___ in diameter.
The catheter may be used for infusion therapy and the tip lies in a midline
position, in the left axillary vein.

The staff radiologist has reviewed the images and the report.
